A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sum-of-Parts research despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet and CosmoGrid experiments, numerical attribution-error analyses, a human distinction study, and cosmological findings.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds MultiRC evaluation, group-mask probing, and further robustness and numerical analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions retain thresholded attention-based group generation, a frozen backbone, sparsemax group selection, and weighted prediction aggregation. The classification and regression loss scaling in v2 Appendix C.7 reappears in v3 Appendix B.3. The BERT application and newly documented implementation details do not establish a changed core algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds MultiRC reading comprehension formulated as binary answer-correctness classification, with ERASER rationale annotations for evaluation. This extends the evaluated coverage from image classification and cosmological image regression to language understanding.

E2.justification: The corresponding ImageNet and CosmoGrid experiments retain their comparator sets and post-hoc conversion procedures. MultiRC and the additional analyses reuse existing comparison methods. Changes to '-F' labels do not establish different baselines.

E3.justification: ImageNet semantic evaluation changes from entropy-based purity to reported IOU. The stated CosmoGrid training budget changes from one epoch to three; v3 also introduces MultiRC training and mask-only probing protocols and random-color occlusion controls. These are reported setting changes, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Equation 50 prints 1 minus IOU, contradicting the metric description and leaving its exact implementation ambiguous.

E4.justification: v3 adds CNN, linear, and ViT probes testing whether group masks encode labels, random-color occlusion robustness tests, and sparsity analyses for CosmoGrid and MultiRC. The existing purity-threshold and fine-step insertion/deletion analyses remain. v2's qualitative random-versus-identity initialization and frozen-versus-finetuned encoder ablations are removed, although the multihead-diversity observation remains.

E5.justification: Both versions report uncertainty alongside results and retain the human study's standard deviations estimated through 1,000 bootstrap resamples. The study still uses ten images and three workers per task. No changed seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is disclosed.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds MultiRC results: SOP's error is 0.366 ± 0.021, tying RISE-F at displayed precision. ImageNet purity results are replaced by IOU results, which are not directly comparable. New faithfulness, probing, and robustness outcomes appear throughout the appendix. Figure 9 revises mean void contributions to Ωm/σ8 from 23.8%/18.5% to 50.7%/41.5%. The existing Table 1 ImageNet errors and CosmoGrid MSE values remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 formally defines SANNs and errors against target functions, introduces dual-certificate lower-bound theorems, and distinguishes these from conjectured exponential trends. It corrects grouped insertion/deletion set conditions and empty-set handling, extends the zero-error construction to general polynomials in Theorem 6, and adds squared-error definitions and least-squares derivations in Appendix A.2.

C1.justification: v2 centers faithful grouped attributions and performance/faithfulness claims on ImageNet and CosmoGrid. v3 recasts the central theoretical claim around performance limitations of per-feature SANNs and expands the positive result to general polynomials. Its empirical contribution now claims state-of-the-art SANN performance across vision and language, materially extending the claim's scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains strong deletion scores through attention rapidly redirecting focus; v3 instead emphasizes deletion tests' bias toward models relying on few features. It adds substantive interpretations concerning label leakage and alignment between learned groups and correlated signals. Explicit training-overhead and accuracy-critical-use caveats from v2's conclusion disappear, while cosmological noise and relative-area qualifications remain in Appendix D.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents evenly spaced query selection for the 20 groups, Gaussian smoothing kernels, and BERT/MultiRC training details. Conversely, v2's AdamW optimizer specification, beta values, weight decay, and no-warmup disclosure are omitted. Hardware, code access, and loss-scaling information remain, sometimes relocated.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is substantially refocused around per-feature versus group-based SANNs and their distinction from prototype and concept models. v3 adds prototype-model references and literature supporting its new evaluations, while removing substantial discussions of grouped-attribution search methods, stability, and human-evaluation approaches. This changes research positioning beyond bibliographic editing.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, theoretical narrative, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Separate attribution-theory and self-explaining-model sections are consolidated, evaluations are reorganized into performance, interpretability, and utility, and substantial method and cosmology material moves between the main text and appendices.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a third dataset, cosmological histograms become box and density plots, and new probing, squared-error, and sparsity displays are added. Algorithm 1 and the main ImageNet faithfulness table move to the appendix. Existing example grids are substantially compressed, and the numerical human-study table is removed while its results remain plotted.

improvement.justification: The added language evaluation and mask-probing/occlusion checks strengthen evidence missing from v2, and corrected group-set conditions repair parts of the original mathematics. The net gain is limited by v3's contradictory IOU formula in Equation 50, Theorems 7–8 confusing an optimizing coefficient vector with an error bound, and removal of optimizer details and explicit applicability caveats.
